messages:
sarah: Heads up — spotted an authorization bug in Console -> Admin -> Quotas. A BillingViewer user in a customer tenant can see org-level usage/cost breakdown. Repro steps below. :eyes:

priya: omg, can you paste the exact request/response?

sarah: repro (sanitized):
```
curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer <user-token>' \ 
  'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/orgs/ORG123/usage?range=30d&group_by=project'

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
{
  "org_total": 12453.12,
  "by_project": [{"project":"p1","cost":12000.00},{"project":"p2","cost":453.12}]
}
```
The caller has role BillingViewer (should NOT see org_total). No errors in response.

mike: that matches what i saw locally. I think this slipped in from last week's RBAC refactor — analytics-service moved the quota/usage endpoint behind the analytics gateway and we accidentally relied on client-side filtering. PR #1423 changed checks to only run in gateway, but the gateway caches permission_evals and a missing cache-key caused the check to be skipped.

carla: sec-oncall, can you triage? Need to confirm scope (prod tenants affected?), whether audit logs recorded the permission decision.

sec-oncall: triaging now. Quick notes: audit logs show the request events, but policy evaluation field is "skipped" for ~300 requests in the last 48h. Looks like the evaluation step returned code 204 from policy service due to a timeout on the KMS signature call. KMS timeouts -> fallback path mistakenly treats as ALLOW. :lock:

infra-bot: deployment note: analytics-service v2.3.1 deployed 2025-10-31T03:12:00Z (commit ab12ef). Related RBAC refactor landed in that release. Rollback window still open for <72h.

priya: proposed mitigation plan (short):
- immediate: add server-side enforcement in analytics-service to mask `org_total` unless `role: billing_admin` or `role: finance_lead`. Emit explicit audit event with decision.
- short term: flip gateway to fail-closed on policy evaluation timeouts.
- medium: add e2e test asserting org-level cost not returned for BillingViewer.
- notify customers and run a data-access audit for last 30d.

mike: i'll open an emergency PR with tests + e2e. cc: @carla for canary in us-west1. Will include a feature-flagged rollback.

carla: oncall accepts. I'll run canary and push to staging now. Also: we need a list of impacted tenants to notify — sec-oncall, can you export logs and check which tenants had >1 org_total exposure?

sec-oncall: running log query now. Using audit index: `service:analytics AND event:usage_query AND policy_evaluation:skipped`. Initial hit ~ 42 tenants. Exporting CSV and creating incident ticket. Also opening Security Review: potential data exposure (cost metadata).

priya: note on KMS: audit events are encrypted at rest. The timeout we saw is from the policy service signing call (key access) — make sure key rotation didn't hit old replicas. I'll coordinate with infra to validate KMS end-to-end and add metric `policy_sign_time_ms`.

mike: remediation timeline: PR in 15m, canary in 30-45m, full rollout in 90m if canary clean. Rollback plan: revert analytics-service to v2.3.0.

carla: tagging @legal and @support for customer comms draft. Priya, sec-oncall — keep the incident ticket updated with audit CSV and timeline.

priya: created checklist and incident runbook entry, pushing to /incidents/ cases. I'll also add Sentry alert for `authorization_failure` and a pager threshold: >5/min per tenant. :thumbsup:

sarah: thanks all. Leaving reproduction details in the incident ticket. Will follow up if we find any exposed external actors.
